parts.problem_md: Do you think access to skilled staff is the most important factor for a service business to consider when deciding where to locate a new branch? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Access to workers with appropriate skills, qualifications and customer service experience **[K]** is often an important factor, but skilled staff can be difficult to find, which could increase recruitment costs. In addition, technology and automation may reduce the need for some staff, reducing the importance of access to skilled labour in some cases **[An]**

Other factors can be equally or more important depending on the situation. Good transport links and proximity to customers **[K]** ensure that clients can access the service easily and conveniently. This is particularly important for services requiring face-to-face interaction such as healthcare or legal advice **[An]**

The importance of access to skilled staff depends on the specific service business and type of service provided. For labour-intensive services, access to qualified workers is crucial, as the branch cannot operate without them **[E]**. Other factors may be more important, though, where services are technology-based or where customer accessibility is key **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Access to skilled staff:
> 
>   - Labour intensive services require access to skilled staff [k], without qualified staff they cannot operate [an]
>   - Can depend on type of workers required [k], basic service staff may be easy to find [an]
> - Other factors might include:
> 
>   - Proximity to customers [k], to ensure sales/revenue can be made [an]
>   - Type of service [k], a specialised service may need to be closer to target customers to build trust/reputation [an]
>   - Access to suppliers/technology [k], so service delivery is not delayed [an]
>   - Availability/cost of suitable premises [k], which could restrict size of operation/limit capacity/increases fixed costs [an]
>   - Government influence or examples e.g. government grants [k], can help reduce costs [an], whereas legal controls could prevent the business from locating in certain areas [an]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Skilled staff may be difficult to find [k], which could increase recruitment costs [an]
>   - Technology and automation can replace some staff [k], reducing the importance of skilled labour in the location decision [an]
>   - Skilled staff is the most important factor if the business is labour intensive, because without qualified staff the new branch cannot deliver quality service [eval], however, other factors would be of greater importance in a technology-based service business [eval]

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> Sarah owns a successful furniture manufacturing business in a rural area. She has 8 full-time employees. The business has made a profit in each of the last 3 years. Sarah wants to expand by opening a second manufacturing facility to take advantage of the economic boom. However, she is concerned that the current location may not be suitable for expansion. The business is struggling to recruit enough skilled workers, and transport costs have been increasing significantly.

**Explain two** reasons why the current location is not suitable for Sarah's manufacturing business expansion
parts.solution_md:
Firstly, the rural location makes it difficult to recruit skilled workers **[K]**. Manufacturing businesses need workers with technical skills and experience **[Ap]**, but rural areas typically have smaller populations and fewer people with the required manufacturing expertise, limiting Sarah's ability to find suitable employees for expansion **[An]**

Secondly, the rural location increases transport costs significantly **[K]**. Manufacturing businesses need to transport raw materials in and finished furniture products out **[Ap]**, but rural locations are often far from suppliers and customers, leading to higher logistics costs that reduce profitability **[An]**

> - Write two developed paragraphs, one for each part of the question
> - For each paragraph:
> 
>   - State a valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply it clearly to the business in the case study → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain the impact using a cause–effect chain → 1 An mark
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Difficulty recruiting workers / lack of skilled labour / small population **[k] **as manufacturing requires technical skills **[ap], **making it hard to expand production capacity **[an]**
>   - High transport costs / distance from suppliers **[k] **as furniture manufacturing requires raw materials like wood** [ap],** increasing total costs and reducing profit margins **[an]**
>   - Distance from customers / markets **[k] **as furniture is bulky to transport** [ap], **leading to higher delivery costs and reduced competitiveness **[an]**
>   - Limited infrastructure / poor road access **[k]**, making it difficult to transport large furniture items **[ap]**, causing delays that may lead to customer dissatisfaction **[an]**
>   - Lack of supporting businesses / suppliers nearby **[k]**, as manufacturing relies on regular deliveries **[ap]**, increasing lead times and inventory costs **[an]**
>   - Limited access to technology / internet connectivity **[k] **needed for modern manufacturing processes **[ap]**, reducing efficiency and competitiveness **[an]**
>   - Higher utility costs / limited power supply **[k] **as manufacturing requires significant electricity **[ap]**, increasing fixed costs **[an]**
>   - Distance from training facilities / colleges **[k] **makes it hard to develop workers' practical skills **[ap]**, limiting productivity improvements **[an]**
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited.
> - The following words are likely to be appropriate for this question:
> 
>   - Manufacturing or examples such as furniture, wood
>   - Rural (area)
>   - 8 (employees)
>   - 2 facilities / second facility
>   - Make a profit in each of the last 3 years
>   - Economic boom

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Vegetable Palace (VP) **

VP was started 10 years ago in country Z. It is a public limited company. VP has a chain of 500 fast-food restaurants that operate across country Z. The VP brand is famous for its vegetarian food, this means none of its meals contain meat.

VP has a head office in Main City where all the directors and senior managers work. There are many barriers to communication. Each VP restaurant has a Manager, an Assistant Manager and 50 employees who cook and serve the meals. Restaurant Managers are often very busy and they are considering delegating some of their tasks to the Assistant Managers.

The ingredients for the restaurants are ordered in bulk by head office and then distributed from its warehouse to each of the restaurants. However, some senior managers think that Restaurant Managers should purchase their own ingredients from local suppliers. This would mean the ingredients would be fresher and would allow variations in the meals served.

VP wants to expand into another country. It will choose between the two countries shown in Appendix 2. VP will also need to decide how to enter a new market in another country. It has the option of forming a joint venture with another business or franchising the VP brand. The choice of finance will need to be considered for the expansion and the amount of finance will depend on the option chosen.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for VP's restaurants **

Choose VP for the finest vegetarian meals. Our service is the fastest possible!

You will receive your meal in less than 5 minutes – guaranteed!

Delicious and varied meals for even the biggest of appetites and all at competitive prices.

New meals are being introduced all the time.

There is a VP restaurant near you – we look forward to serving you soon.

**Appendix 2 **

**Summary of the two possible countries that VP could choose to locate its new restaurants.**

|   | **Country A** | **Country B** |
|---|---|---|
| **Raw materials** | Average variable cost \$6 per meal | Average variable cost \$2 per meal |
| **Labour** | Low unemployment \$10 per hour for each employee | High unemployment \$5 per hour for each employee |
| **Market** | Many competitors Average price per meal = \$20 | Few competitors Average price per meal = \$10 |

**Appendix 3 **

**Email from VP’s Managing Director to VP’s Marketing Director **

To: VP’s Marketing Director

From: VP’s Managing Director

Date: 31 March 2023

Re: Economic changes in country Z

Did you see the news this morning that interest rates will be raised from 3% to 5% later today? This will have several effects on our business in country Z.

The news also said that the exchange rate in country Z has depreciated. We will have to consider how this will affect our business, especially as we import 30% of our ingredients into country Z.

There are also new legal controls being introduced that mean we have to list all the ingredients used in each of our meals on the menu. We do reprint menus every time we change the meals, but it is something to consider.

Speak later today.

Using Appendix 2 and other information, consider the two countries VP could choose to locate its new restaurants. Which country should VP choose? **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2023-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf) when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
In Country A the average price per meal is \$20, which is double that of Country B **[Ap]**. This could lead to high revenue and profit margins for VP **[An]**. The many competitors **[Ap]** suggests there is strong demand for fast food restaurants and potential for growth **[An]**. However, Country A has higher costs, with average variable costs of \$6 per meal and wages of \$10 per hour **[Ap]**. The low unemployment rate **[Ap] **may make it difficult for VP to recruit staff for its new restaurants. As good customer service could be an important way for VP to stand out against the many rivals, this is particularly concerning **[An]**

Country B has much lower costs, with average variable costs of just \$2 per meal and wages of \$5 per hour **[Ap]**. This would allow VP to keep its prices competitive at \$10 per meal **[Ap] **while maintaining healthy profit margins **[An]**. The high unemployment rate would make it easier for VP to find workers **[An]**. However, the few competitors **[Ap]** could indicate lower demand for fast food or an untapped market opportunity. This is a risk for VP **[An]**

VP should locate its new restaurants in Country B **[E]**. While revenue may be lower initially due to the \$10 average meal price, the significantly lower costs **[Ap] **will allow for higher profit margins **[E]**. The lack of competition provides an opportunity for VP to establish itself as a market leader. Country A's higher costs and competitive market **[Ap] **make it a riskier option, despite the potential for higher revenue **[E]**. By choosing Country B, VP can build a strong presence in an emerging market while keeping costs low **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Town A**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Highest gross profit → profit \$140 000 after expenses
>     - Franchise fee is the smallest share of gross profit → more retained earnings
>     - Shorter 5-year lease → flexibility to relocate
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Highest total expenses \$260 000 → greater cost burden
>     - Highest rent of the three towns → fixed cost pressure
> - **Town B**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Wages and salaries \$10 000 lower than Town A → total costs \$110 000 pre-franchise fees
>     - Gross profit \$100 000 above Town C → stronger contribution to covering fees
>     - Profit \$80 000 after expenses
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Total expenses \$220 000 → thinner margins than Town A
>     - Lease shorter than Town C → less long-term security
> - **Town C**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Lowest total costs \$83 000 pre-franchise fees → smallest expense base
>     - Lowest total expenses \$173 000 → more buffer if sales dip
>     - Cheapest heating and lighting costs
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Longest 15-year lease → high risk if performance is poor
>     - Lowest annual profit \$27 000 → limited return potential
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Town A delivers maximum profit now and retains more earnings → best for short-term gains
>   - Town B balances profit and cost with moderate lease security → suitable for a medium-risk strategy
>   - Town C offers lowest costs and longest lease but generates the smallest profit → ideal only for a long-term, risk-tolerant plan

**Gemma’s Jewels (GJ)**

Gemma set up GJ as a sole trader 5 years ago in country Z. She started by selling rings and bracelets from a rented shop. She used her own savings to start the business. The first year was successful. After this first year Gemma decided to expand by selling more expensive items of jewellery. Gemma thinks it is important to set clear business objectives. She wants her business to increase sales by 10% each year and to increase market share.

As the business grew Gemma needed more finance for a computer, inventory and working capital to avoid liquidity problems. She decided to convert the business to a private limited company and sell shares to members of her family. Gemma still owns more than 50% of the shares in GJ.

In 2019, Gemma purchased a franchise from Beautywise Jewellery. This means GJ is now only able to sell Beautywise products in its shop. GJ has to purchase all of its inventory from Beautywise and in addition pay 20% of gross profit to Beautywise. More details about the franchise are in the advertisement in Appendix 1.

Gemma has developed a website so customers can order online. Customers can also download a mobile (cell) phone app to view and order jewellery.

Gemma plans to open a second shop as a Beautywise franchise in a nearby town. She has to decide which method of sales promotion to use. GJ needs to recruit a manager for the new shop. The manager will be responsible for operating the shop and making most of the decisions about which items of inventory to buy. The manager will also need to ensure excellent customer service is provided and that the new employees are motivated and working efficiently.

**Appendix 1 **

**Advertisement for Beautywise Jewellery Franchise**

**Become a franchisee to sell Beautywise Jewellery and improve your chances of success!!**

What we offer you:

- Be the only shop in your area that sells Beautywise jewellery
- Beautywise will advertise nationally on television and in newspapers
- Help and advice on decoration of the shop and training for employees and the franchisee
- Ethically sourced jewellery imported especially for Beautywise
- The franchise fee is just \$50 000 per year!

**Appendix 2 **

**Newspaper article- Daily News **

**External factors affecting the jewellery market in country Z**

The demand for jewellery in country Z is likely to be affected by some recent changes. Consumers are becoming more aware of the ethical issues involved in jewellery production in some countries. The exchange rate of the currency of country Z is likely to depreciate over the next 12 months. The Government is planning changes to tax rates which might reduce the effects of the current economic boom.

**Appendix 3 **

**Information on three possible locations for the new shop**

| **Annual costs** | **Town A** | **Town B** | **Town C** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shop rent | \$45 000 per year for 5 years | \$35 000 per year for 10 years | \$20 000 per year for 15 years |
| Wages and salaries | \$80 000 | \$70 000 | \$60 000 |
| Heating and lighting | \$5 000 | \$5 000 | \$3 000 |
| Estimated gross profit | \$400 000 | \$300 000 | \$200 000 |

Note: Franchise fee is \$50 000 per year and 20% of gross profit is paid to Beautywise.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the **three** towns for the new shop shown in Appendix 3. Recommend which town Gemma should choose for the location of the new shop. **Justify **your answer.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf) when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Town A has the highest estimated gross profit at \$400,000 **[Ap]**, which would allow Gemma's Jewels to pay the franchise fee and still make a healthy profit **[An]**. However, it also has the highest rent at \$45,000 per year and the shortest lease of only 5 years **[Ap]**. The wages and heating costs are also highest here, leading to total costs of \$130,000 per year **[Ap]** before franchise payments. These factors are a risk if the business takes time to establish itself **[An]**

Town B offers a balance between profit potential and costs. The estimated gross profit of \$300,000 **[Ap]**  is less than Town A but still substantial **[An]**. The rent of \$35,000 per year for a 10-year lease **[Ap]** provides more stability than Town A. Wages are \$10,000 lower than Town A, and total costs before franchise payments are \$110,000 per year **[Ap]**. This could allow for steady growth over time.

Town C has the lowest estimated gross profit at \$200,000 **[Ap]**, but also the lowest costs. The rent is only \$20,000 per year for a long 15-year lease **[Ap]**, providing the most stability. However, the lower gross profit means less money to cover the franchise fee and other costs, potentially limiting profitability **[An]**

Gemma should choose Town B **[E] **as it provides the best opportunity for sustainable growth. It offers good profit potential, has manageable costs and a reasonable lease length **[E]**. Town A's higher costs and short lease **[Ap] **make it too risky, while Town C's lower sales potential **[Ap]** could make it difficult to be profitable after franchise payments **[E]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think legal controls are the most important factor for a manufacturing business to consider when deciding which country to locate its operations in? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
A country's legal controls may require changes to production methods **[K]**, such as reducing emissions or prohibiting the use of certain components. This could incur significant costs to upgrade facilities or source alternative supplies **[An]**, which may not be required in another country

However, other factors like access to labour **[K]** could also be crucial. A country that offers adequate access to skilled workers could help reduce costs as they would require less training and may be more productive than those in a country that lacks this resource **[An]**

Legal controls are an important factor for manufacturing businesses to consider when choosing a country to locate in, but they may not be the most important **[E]. **Legal controls can disrupt or even prevent a business using established production techniques, but factors like access to resources and labour may be more important as they directly impact the ability to produce goods efficiently and profitably **[E]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think access to labour is the most important factor for a manufacturing business to consider when deciding where to locate a new factory? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Access to workers with appropriate skills, experience and qualifications **[K]** is often an important factor, but skilled labour can be difficult to find, which could increase recruitment costs. In addition, machinery that can replace labour may be available, reducing the importance of access to labour in some cases **[An]**

Other factors can be equally or more important depending on the situation. Good transport links and proximity to the market **[K] **ensure that products can be moved efficiently and quickly to customers. This is particularly important for perishable goods such as food **[An]**

The importance of access to labour depends on the specific manufacturing business and product. For labour-intensive production, access to workers is crucial, as the factory cannot operate without them **[E]**. Other factors may be more important, though, where production is capital-intensive or where speed of delivery is key** [E]**

>   - Can depend on type of workers required [k], unskilled workers may be easy to find [an]
> 
>   - Good transport links [k], to ensure products arrive / sent when needed [an]
>   - Proximity to market [k], to ensure sales / revenue can be made [an]
>   - Type of product [k], a fragile / heavy product may need to be closer to customers to reduce risk of damage / cost [an]
